claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, off-axis points gamma_j - i delta at distinct heights and one distance delta, multiplicities m_j, bandwidth Lam, b = delta Lam, theta_j = Lam (gamma_j - gamma_0), w_j = m_j exp(-i Lam gamma_j), nu_r = sum w_j theta_j^r, k the least r with nu_r nonzero (k <= n-1, independent of gamma_0), c = sum m_j |theta_j|^(k+1): | 2 delta (2b)^k sqrt(Q(Lam)) - |nu_k| sqrt(gamma(2k+2, 2b))/k! | <= c sqrt((2k+3)!)/((k+1)! 2b), so ||B_Lam||_HS = (e^b/(sqrt2 b)) |nu_k| sqrt((2k+1)!)/(k! (2b)^k) (1 + O(1/b)) + O(M).
claim.assessment: Working proof: Taylor expansion of the exponential sum at the endpoint of the range, where the weight u e^(-2 delta u) concentrates, and the triangle inequality in the weighted norm. Gives the exact order b^(-2k) of the single-bandwidth cancellation among pairs at one distance, with its leading constant. Unequal distances are outside the statement.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Settles, for equal distances, the order of the single-bandwidth loss of a cluster in the Gram model, which earlier entries left between two exponents; no consequence about zeros, the model's premise being unavailable.
significance.next_action: None on the route; unequal distances and the largest order for simple points are undetermined.

claim.summary: In the setting of the endpoint moment order with heights in increasing order: k = n-1 if and only if every gap is an odd multiple of pi/Lam and m_j is proportional to the product over l != j of 1/|gamma_j - gamma_l| (the divided-difference weights); if all heights lie in an open interval of length pi/Lam then k = 0.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the solution space of n-1 vanishing moments is spanned by the divided-difference weights, real with alternating signs, and positive multiplicities with unimodular phases match them exactly when consecutive phases are opposite.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Identifies the configurations with the largest single-bandwidth cancellation, order b^(-2(n-1)), and shows that points closer than pi/Lam do not cancel to leading order.

claim.summary: For every finite conjugation-closed configuration Z in the complete-grid Gram model with real even window phi supported in [-Lam/2,Lam/2]: ||G_Z||_HS^2 = ||phi||_2^-4 int_{-Lam}^{Lam} (phi^2*phi^2)(s) |S_Z(s)|^2 ds, S_Z(s) = sum_z m_z e^{-isz} = sum_real m e^{-is gamma} + 2 sum_j m_j e^{-is gamma_j} cosh(delta_j s).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof from the bilinear Gram identity and conjugation invariance. Identifies the Hilbert-Schmidt norm at bandwidth Lam with a weighted mean square of the zero sum over |log x| <= Lam. Abstract statement about configurations; no estimate for zeta zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Makes explicit that a second-moment premise at bandwidth Lam is a mean-square bound for the exponential sum over the points; expected to be the classical mean-square form of pair-correlation sums, novelty not claimed.
significance.next_action: Use for the cluster question: lower bounds for the mean square with positive integer coefficients.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; trapezoid-rule control against grid sums on 22 configurations agrees to the stated tolerance.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, n = 2^k simple off-axis points at equal distance delta with heights sum_{i in S} q_i pi/Lam0 (q_i odd, distinct subset sums), b = delta Lam0: ||B_{Lam0}||_HS^2 <= (e^{2b}/(2b^2)) (2k+1)! prod_i (q_i pi/(2b))^2 + 3 n^2, which is O_k(b^{-2k}) times 2 n kappa^2 for q_i = 3^(i-1); so no single-bandwidth bound ||B||_HS^2 >= c b^{-A} sum m_j^2 kappa_j^2 with fixed c, A holds uniformly in n for simple points.
claim.assessment: Refutation, by an explicit family and a short proof (product formula, vanishing of order k at the end of the interval), of a single-bandwidth lower bound with a fixed power loss. The case k = 1 is the two-pair cancellation. The exact single-bandwidth loss between exponents 2 log_2 n and 2(n-1) is not determined.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows that at one bandwidth close off-line pairs with simple points can cancel by more than any fixed power of delta*Lam; motivates varying the bandwidth.
significance.next_action: None on this route; the resonance-free bandwidth theorem makes the exact single-bandwidth loss immaterial.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, configuration {+-i delta, t +- i delta}: ||G_Z||_HS^2 = 4 + 4 kappa^2 + 4 sinc^2(t Lam/2) + 4 Re sinc^2((t+2i delta)Lam/2), kappa = sinh(b)/b, b = delta Lam; at t = pi/Lam and b >= pi/2 this is at most 4 + 16/pi^2 + 3 pi^2 kappa^2 / b^2, so no absolute c > 0 gives ||G_Z||_HS^2 >= c sum_j (kappa_j^2 + 1) over off-axis pairs.
claim.assessment: Refutation, by an exact identity, of the additive lower bound that would extend solitary amplification to several off-line pairs at constant cost. The loss shown is a factor of order b^-2 for two pairs; the loss for many close pairs is not computed.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, off-axis points at pairwise distinct heights with least gap g, multiplicities m_j, M = sum m_j, largest distance delta_* attained with multiplicity m_*, m' the largest multiplicity among the other points: for Lam1 >= 1/delta_* and h >= (4 pi/sqrt 3) sqrt(m'/m_*)/g, some Lam in [Lam1, Lam1 + 2h] has ||B_Lam||_HS >= (sqrt2/4) m_* e^(delta_* Lam)/(delta_* Lam) - M.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the earlier theorem's average over the bandwidth taken with a triangular weight, whose transform at complex frequency is bounded by 4/(h nu^2), and only the cross terms with the largest pair are bounded, the rest being dropped as a square (the reviewer's improvement of the first draft). The range 14.5 sqrt(m'/m_*)/g replaces 4 M^2/(g m_*^2); neither contains the other. Conditional on an unavailable second-moment premise for any consequence about zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows that in the Gram model a cluster of close off-line pairs shows its largest pair at some bandwidth in every range of length of order sqrt(m'/m_*)/g; no consequence about zeros, the model's premise being unavailable.
significance.next_action: None on the route; whether the factor sqrt(m'/m_*) is necessary is undecided.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, off-axis points at pairwise distinct heights with least gap g, total multiplicity M, largest distance delta_* attained with multiplicity m_*: for Lam1 >= 1/delta_* and H >= 4 M^2/(g m_*^2) (H = 0 if n = 1) some Lam in [Lam1, Lam1+H] has ||B_Lam||_HS >= (sqrt2/4) m_* e^{delta_* Lam}/(delta_* Lam) - M >= (sqrt2/2) m_* kappa_Lam(delta_*) - M. No condition on the other delta_j and no separation relative to delta; the benchmark is the single largest pair.
claim.assessment: Working proof: split off e^{delta_* s}, mean value of an exponential sum with nonincreasing positive amplitudes by integration by parts, average over the bandwidth, triangle inequality in the weighted norm. For configurations at distinct heights it bounds the largest delta from a second-moment bound over a range of bandwidths of length 4M^2/(g m_*^2), which depends on the configuration and can far exceed Lam1; how short the range can be is open, and unverified examples indicate that length of order 1/g is necessary. Conditional on an unavailable second-moment premise for any consequence about zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows that cancellation among close off-line pairs in the Gram model is a resonance at particular bandwidths. With the real configuration bound the route is a reformulation in the model and supplies no estimate.
significance.next_action: Determine the necessary and sufficient length of the bandwidth range: verify the equally spaced examples and prove the version with H of order 1/g for equal delta.
